# Drag release into a restored inline prompt

Inputs are the independent manually authored OPC controls in
`../empty-control-prompt-pointer`, generated by
`tools/empty_control_prompt_pointer_fixture.py`. Fresh disposable copies were
opened in the reference application on September 29, 2026, at 100% zoom in a 946x536
window. The input copies were saved over to retain the native outcomes;
original fixture inputs remain unchanged.

Each input starts with A, an empty persistent rich-text control, and a suffix.
Clicking between A and the suffix exposes the `letters` control label. Drag
from that same position to the target below, release, type Q, and save:

| Input | Entry and drag start | Release | Saved result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tail.docx | (113,254) | (220,254), past XYZ | AQ |
| soft.docx | (114,253) | (220,253), inside THREE | AQ FOUR FIVE SIX SEVEN EIGHT NINE TEN |
| break.docx | (113,254) | (220,254), first line past XYZ | AQ, manual break, UVW |

The soft control uses Courier New 12pt and a 144pt writing width. Before
restoration its first line reads AONE TWO THREE FOUR. The resulting suffix
proves that the selection ends at the originally targeted word, rather than
at the end of the original visual line or paragraph. The manual-break case
independently preserves the next line. In all three saved outputs the inline
control is removed by replacement. `record_empty_control_prompt_drag.py`
extracts actual XML text and control counts, infers the original selected
suffix boundary from the surviving text, and binds input/output hashes.

The rule applies when a completed ordinary drag out of an empty persistent
inline rich-text owner restores its prompt, and the physical release point
then hits that same restored owner. The reference application selects from its start through the
end of the word targeted before restoration. Short prompts whose restored
area does not cover the release point retain the collapsed outside caret
established by `../empty-control-drag`.

The unchanged viewer selects only the prompt: the tail regression receives
[1,360] instead of the native [1,363]. Browser checks use actual pointer events
with one and twelve moves at zoom 1 and .75, saved-native selection boundaries,
replacement ownership, untouched parts, two-step undo/redo, and reopening.

ECMA-376 Part 1 §§17.5.2.26/31 and 17.5.2.25/39 define SDT/content and
placeholder markup; they do not prescribe this mouse transition. These are
native editing-compatibility controls, not a demonstrated standards conflict.
Shift-click and same-offset edge exits remain unresolved; corpus document #137 is
not marked complete by this repair.
